ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–90 cm. It is greyish-brown with dark, paired cross-bands and a distinctive V-shaped mark on the head. It possesses enlarged, blade-like rear teeth for egg-eating.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Oligodon taeniolatus* is the distinct, V-shaped or arrow-headed dark marking located on the top of its head.
ai.habitat: The Streaked Kukri Snake inhabits diverse environments, including dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and rocky hills, ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Streaked Kukri snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs, allowing it to consume the contents efficiently.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon taeniolatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs between March and June in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Streaked Kukri Snake is found across much of India, from the Himalayan foothills to the southern peninsula, typically inhabiting plains and hills up to 2,000m.
